Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 2. Routine and fun
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Daily routine
- Materials: Clock, routine timeline, survey sheet, COSYmanuals 'telling the time', 'present simple', and 'adverbs of frequency' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• detail full daily schedules with time prepositions
• use frequency adverbs in complex routines
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles present simple, telling the time, and frequency adverbs.

Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

shower — a wash under falling water. Example: I take a shower every morning.
always — every time. Example: I always drink water.
usually — most of the time. Example: She usually walks to work.
sometimes — on some occasions. Example: I sometimes watch films.
never — not at any time. Example: He never drinks coffee.
wake up — to stop sleeping. Example: I wake up at seven.
breakfast — the first meal of the day. Example: I have breakfast at eight.
work — a job or activity you do. Example: I work in an office.
evening — the later part of the day. Example: Good evening, Mrs Brown.
schedule — a plan of times and activities. Example: My schedule is very busy.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I always wake up at six. (routine with frequency)
• I usually take a shower. (routine with frequency)
• I sometimes work late. (routine with frequency)
• I never skip breakfast. (routine with frequency)
• After work, I... (sequencing the day)
• My schedule is busy. (describing the day)

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use time expressions to say when you do something.

Form:
Telling the time: What time is it? It's seven o'clock. It's half past seven. It's quarter past seven. It's quarter to eight. Use 'at' + time: at seven o'clock.

Examples:
• I wake up at seven o'clock.
• The class starts at half past nine.
• We have lunch at quarter past twelve.
• She goes to bed at ten o'clock.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
It's 7:00. It's ___ o'clock.
It's 7:30. It's half ___ seven.
It's 7:45. It's quarter ___ eight.
I wake up ___ seven o'clock.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I wake up at ...
• I have breakfast at ...
• I go to bed at ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What time do you wake up?
• What time do you start work or school?
• What time do you go to bed?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your day with times.
• Write three sentences about a family member's day with times.
Reading: Daily routine

My daily routine starts early. I always wake up at six and take a shower. I usually have breakfast at seven. I sometimes work late in the evening. I never skip lunch. After work, I go home and relax. My schedule is busy, but I like my routine. What is your daily routine like?
What time does the writer wake up?
How often does the writer work late?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What is your daily routine?
B: I always wake up at six thirty. I usually have breakfast at seven.
A: Do you work late?
B: Sometimes, but I never work on Sunday.
A: What do you do in the evening?
B: I usually relax and read.
What time does the speaker wake up?
What does the speaker never do?
Speaking task: Compare your daily routine with your partner's. Find three differences.

• What time do you wake up?
• Do you always have breakfast?
• Do you ever work late?
• What do you do in the evening?
• Is your schedule busy?
Role-play: You are a time-management consultant. Interview a client about their routine and suggest two changes.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your full daily routine with times and frequency.
Model: I always ... I usually ... I sometimes ... I never ...
